about.title: About New York City Public Schools
about.content: New York City Public Schools, also known as NYCPS, serves students across New York City. The NYCPS school year calendar is used for districtwide planning across 3-K, Pre-K, elementary, middle, high school, K-12, 6-12, and District 75 school communities.

about.title: How to Use This NYCPS Calendar
about.content: Use this page for citywide school calendar planning, including the first day of school, school holidays, recess periods, parent-teacher conferences, Regents Administration windows, clerical days, and the last day of school. Families should confirm private, parochial, charter, NYC Early Education Center, Family Childcare, school-specific, athletic, testing, and graduation dates directly with their school.

planningTips.title: NYCPS Calendar Reminders Before Making Plans
content: Confirm whether each parent-teacher conference or early dismissal date applies to your child's school level before arranging pickup.
Check the official NYCPS calendar and school notices before booking nonrefundable travel, childcare, or transportation.
Treat Regents Administration windows as high school planning dates unless your school says they affect a broader schedule.
Watch for NYCPS emergency updates, because remote learning or closure decisions may change during severe weather or other disruptions.

customSections.label: About NYCPS Calendar Structure
customSections.content: The NYCPS calendar is a citywide school year calendar for 3-K through grade 12, but several dates depend on school level. Elementary, middle, high school, K-12, 6-12, and District 75 parent-teacher conference dates are listed separately, and some affected students are dismissed three hours early. The calendar also identifies Regents Administration windows, clerical days, Anniversary Day or Chancellor's Conference Day, and recess periods. Families should use the official NYCPS calendar for citywide dates and then verify school-specific events with their child's school.

customSections.label: NYCPS Calendar vs School-Specific Calendars
customSections.content: The NYCPS school year calendar is the right source for districtwide dates such as the first day of school, winter recess, midwinter recess, spring recess, school holidays, and the last day of school. It does not replace school-specific notices for private, parochial, charter, NYCEEC, Family Childcare, athletics, graduation ceremonies, testing, field trips, or local events.

customSections.label: How We Collect NYCPS Calendar Data
customSections.content: MySchoolDates reviews the official New York City Public Schools calendar and extracts student dates, holidays, recess periods, parent-teacher conferences, Regents windows, clerical days, and other school-year planning dates. The page links back to NYCPS so families can verify updates before making final childcare, travel, transportation, or work plans.

districtFaqs.q: Which New York City Public Schools calendar does this page summarize?
districtFaqs.a: This page summarizes the official NYCPS school year calendar for 3-K through grade 12 for the listed school years.

districtFaqs.q: Does the NYCPS calendar apply to charter schools?
districtFaqs.a: Not necessarily. NYCPS states that private, parochial, charter, NYC Early Education Center, and Family Childcare families should contact their child's school for calendar information.

districtFaqs.q: Are NYCPS parent-teacher conference dates the same for every school?
districtFaqs.a: No. The NYCPS calendar notes that individual school parent-teacher conference dates might be different, and your child's teacher will work with you to schedule your conference.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify New York City Public Schools calendar updates?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official NYCPS calendar page and school announcements for final confirmation. MySchoolDates is an independent reference and is not affiliated with New York City Public Schools.
